schemes.english_name: Applied Integrated Research (AIR) capstone (formerly Applied Management Research)
schemes.description: MBA capstone option in which a team of 5 MBA students consults for an external client organisation (company, government agency or non-profit), doing strategic analysis and market research and delivering executive-level recommendations over about 2.5 months. The client engages without a participation fee.

schemes.participation_data: 'One out of four students in the Full-Time MBA Class of 2026 chose AIR' (percentage, not a count) [2].
schemes.unresolved: Currency inferred from Class of 2026 cohort statements; the pages give no explicit academic year. Credit value not retrieved.

profile_md: UCLA's verified provision sits mostly in professional schools plus one university-wide route. In UCLA Anderson, the Applied Integrated Research (AIR) capstone puts teams of 5 MBA students to work as consultants for an external company, agency or non-profit for about 2.5 months, and the MSBA Applied Analytics Project (a 10-week team project that serves as the comprehensive exam) uses client-supplied data and named client contacts. AIR is one of several MBA capstone options, so it is elective within the programme; the MSBA project appears compulsory but its page is undated. The Center for Community Engagement runs the Community Engagement and Social Change minor, open to undergraduates in any major, whose two-quarter capstone research is conducted in collaboration with a community partner (2026 posters published), but whether it is done in teams is not stated. Luskin's MURP Client Project is a compulsory second-year capstone with nonprofit and public-agency clients (about 30 students in 2026), though it appears individual. The Master of Engineering ENGR 299 capstone is a compulsory team project, but industry sponsors only 'may' be included. Nothing qualifying was verified in sciences, arts or law. Provision is distributed rather than institution-wide, and the evidence is largely undated for engineering and the MSBA project.
gaps: Further Anderson options (ASG, GSIC, FEiSty, TTC, BCC) and Epicenter Innovation Challenge need page-level checks; MPP Applied Policy Project only evidenced by 2017-18 handbook; undergraduate engineering and CS capstones have no sponsor evidence; no results for sciences, humanities departments, arts, law, public health; participation counts largely unpublished. AIR and MSBA pages were read only to 100,000 characters.
